Article Title: “I don’t believe men should compete against women”: Sophie Cunningham lands huge support from popular Hollywood star amid transgender debate in sports
Article Text:
Sophie Cunningham. Image via: Michael Hickey/ Getty Images

Hugh Laurie extends support for Sophie Cunningham amid trans athlete debate

Sophie Cunningham's comments extended the debate

How the league and other players are responding

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham picked up an unlikely ally this week when actor Hugh Laurie publicly backed her stance on transgender athletes in women's sports. The Indiana Fever guard has spent weeks defending comments she made about protecting girls and women in competition, and Laurie's entry into the debate on Aug. 11 pushed the conversation into the entertainment world.The exchange started with a dry post about basketball and ended with Laurie stating his position directly, then naming Cunningham by name.Laurie opened the discussion on Aug. 9 with an observation about how rare it is for a man to reach seven feet tall, framing professional basketball as a sport where almost everyone is unusually built. Writer and comedian Graham Linehan pushed back, calling that approach "cowardly" in a post he later deleted, and asked Laurie to state his views outright.Laurie did not soften his answer. He wrote, "I don't believe men should compete against women," and made clear he thought his position had already been obvious. When Linehan pressed further and asked if he backed Cunningham specifically, Laurie confirmed it, “You started it. ‘Cowardly’ to ‘f*ck off’ is the going rate of exchange around here. And yes, I support Sophie Cunningham. And you, some of the time”. Linehan later apologized for what he called his own knee-jerk reaction and credited Laurie's early comedy work as an influence on his career.Cunningham's side of the story started weeks earlier, in a wide-ranging ESPN profile published July 21 that framed her as supportive of restrictions on transgender participation in girls' and women's sports.She pushed back on any suggestion that her position came from animosity toward transgender people, insisting she was not motivated by hate. She said girls competing in sports today "shouldn't have to go against biological men."Asked about the backlash the following day, Cunningham told reporters she stood by what she said and considered it a matter of common sense, according to video shared by IndyStar Sports. The 29-year-old described her politics as centrist and said assumptions about her views had outpaced anything she actually said.The debate reached the WNBA's front office on Aug. 12, when a task force of team presidents and general managers discussed transgender participation alongside online abuse directed at players. No new eligibility rules came out of the meeting. The league said afterward, "There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA," while also condemning efforts to use the issue to demean people.The 2026 collective bargaining agreement limits WNBA rosters to players who are women but does not define the term further, and no transgender woman has played in the league. Views inside the sport vary. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve has argued for a more inclusive approach, and Storm center Stefanie Dolson has voiced support for transgender rights.The players' union has said it wants to avoid turning athletes into political pawns. Cunningham's own teammate, Caitlin Clark, has stayed out of the policy fight entirely, saying that call belongs to the leagues and governing bodies.Commentator Tim Young, addressing Laurie's willingness to speak out, told Fox News Digital, "Laurie can't be canceled," pointing to the actor's standing as a reason he faced less risk than a less established performer would.Where the WNBA's task force goes next, and whether Cunningham's comments shape any future policy conversation, remains open. For now, the league has drawn a clear line: no rule change, but no end to the discussion either.
Article Summary: Hugh laurie publicly backs sophie cunningham's stance on transgender athletes in women's sports. The indiana fever guard has spent weeks defending comments she made about protecting girls and women in competition. The debate reached the wnba's front office on aug. 12, but no new eligibility rules came out of the meeting.

Article Title: Where is Terrel Williams now after Prichard Colon fight? What happened to his boxing career
Article Text:
Where is Terrel Williams now after Prichard Colon fight? What happened to his boxing career

What happened to Terrel Williams after Prichard Colon fight?

What did Terrel Williams say about Prichard Colon?

Where is Terrel Williams now?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Terrel Williams has kept a low profile since the 2015 fight that changed Prichard Colon’s life. Williams beat Colon by disqualification in the ninth round in Fairfax, Virginia, but Colon suffered a serious brain injury soon after and spent 221 days in a coma. Colon died on August 13, 2026, at 33, more than a decade after the fight. His death has brought fresh attention to the boxer who shared the ring with him that night. So, where is Terrel Williams now, and what happened to his boxing career? Those questions remain difficult to answer.Williams was unbeaten when he entered the ring against Colon on October 17, 2015. He won the fight after Colon’s corner removed his gloves at the end of the ninth round, believing the scheduled 10-round bout was over. The Premier Boxing Champions record confirms Williams won by disqualification after knocking Colon down twice in the ninth.The Washington Post reported that Colon had complained about punches to the back of his head during the bout. Williams was deducted a point in the seventh round for a rabbit punch. After the fight, Colon became dizzy and vomited in his dressing room before collapsing. He was taken to Inova Fairfax Hospital and needed emergency surgery for bleeding on the brain.Williams did not return to the ring for two years. ESPN reported in 2017 that his comeback was being planned after he had stayed away from boxing since the Colon fight. He returned in November that year and won by knockout against Rosemberg Gomez.Williams spoke about the emotional effect of the fight and made clear that he never wanted Colon to suffer such an injury.“I pray for Prichard every single day. I don’t wish nothing but peace and health for that man. It’s been hard on me, too. I didn’t want that to happen to him. I was just trying to win a fight. My life changed that night, and it will never be the same,” the boxer said.The Los Angeles Times also reported shortly after the fight that Williams was deeply affected by Colon’s condition. He said he felt compassion for Colon and his family and was focused on hoping the young boxer would recover.Williams later returned to boxing, but the comeback was short. His record shows four fights after the 2015 bout. He won three of them, including the 2017 comeback, before losing to Thomas Dulorme by unanimous decision on September 21, 2019.Williams is retired from professional boxing. The World Boxing Association lists his final record as 18-1 with 13 knockouts, while his last recorded fight came against Dulorme in 2019.There is little reliable public information about Williams’ life since retirement. He has largely stayed away from interviews and the boxing spotlight, and recent reporting has described him as difficult to reach. There is no clear public record showing that he has returned to boxing or taken on a major public role in the sport.That makes his present whereabouts difficult to confirm. The Colon fight remained the defining event of Williams’ career. More than 10 years later, the fight is again being discussed after Colon’s death at 33. The circumstances of Colon’s death have not been publicly detailed by his family or medical team, according to current reports.

Williams beat colon by disqualification in the ninth round in fairfax, virginia, but colon suffered a serious brain injury soon after and spent 221 days in a coma. Colon died on august 13, 2026, at 33, more than a decade after the fight.

Article Title: Did Terrel Williams apologize to Prichard Colon’s parents? The ‘rabbit punches’ dispute resurfaces after his death
Article Text:
Did Terrel Williams apologize to Prichard Colon’s parents? The ‘rabbit punches’ dispute resurfaces after his death

Terrel Williams never gave Prichard Colon’s family a formal apology

What happened between Prichard Colon and Terrel Williams in 2015?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Prichard Colon’s death has brought fresh attention to the 2015 fight that left the Puerto Rican boxer with a life-changing brain injury. Colon died on August 13, 2026, aged 33, nearly 11 years after facing Terrel Williams at EagleBank Arena in Virginia. One question that has stayed around the fight is whether Williams ever apologized to Colon or his parents, Richard and Nieves Colon, for the punches to the back of his head. There is no public record of a formal apology. Williams has, however, spoken about his regret, said he prays for Colon and described how the fight changed his own life.Williams has never publicly said that he formally apologized to Prichard Colon or his parents. However, he has spoken about the emotional impact of the fight and what happened to Colon.In a 2018 interview with RingTV, Williams said: “I pray for Prichard every single day. I don’t wish nothing but peace and health for that man. It’s been hard on me, too. I didn’t want that to happen to him. I was just trying to win a fight. My life changed that night, and it will never be the same.”That was not the same as a direct apology to the Colon family.The Washington Post also reported in 2019 that Williams wanted to speak with the family but believed that conversation would not happen. He said the incident had affected both his and Colon’s lives.Williams had also tried to visit Colon in the hospital after the fight, according to The Washington Post. He said he was advised against making the visit. The report said Williams knew Nieves Colon blamed him for what happened to her son and that he continued to pray for Prichard.The family’s anger remained. In 2017, Richard and Nieves Colon filed a lawsuit seeking more than $50 million over the injuries suffered during the fight, naming ringside physician Richard Ashby and the promoters.Colon and Williams met on October 17, 2015. Colon entered the fight with a 16-0 record, including 13 knockouts. During the bout, Colon complained about punches to the back of his head, known as rabbit punches.Referee Joe Cooper deducted a point from Williams in the seventh round after one such punch. But more punches to the back of Colon’s head followed, including one later in the fight that was not called a foul.The ninth round became the turning point. Williams knocked Colon down twice. A misunderstanding in Colon’s corner then led to the fighter being disqualified before the 10th round. After returning to his dressing room, Colon became dizzy, vomited and eventually lost consciousness. He was taken to hospital and underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain.Colon spent 221 days in a coma and never returned to boxing. His condition required years of full-time care. He died on August 13, 2026.Williams’ role in the incident was also investigated by Virginia’s Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation. The investigation did not result in disciplinary action against Williams, referee Joe Cooper or ringside doctor Richard Ashby.So, while Williams has repeatedly expressed regret and said he wanted peace and health for Colon, there is no public evidence that he ever made a formal apology to Colon’s parents. The death of Prichard Colon has once again brought that unresolved part of the story into focus.
Article Summary: Prichard colon’s death has brought fresh attention to the 2015 fight that left the puerto rican boxer with a life-changing brain injury. One question that has stayed around the fight is whether williams ever apologized to colon or his parents, richard and nieves colon, for the punches to the back of his head.

Article Title: Inspiring story on fatherhood: "Part of being a great father is being a great example of doing what it takes to take care of your family" - How Tom Brady's children became the heart of his life after
Article Text:
Tom Brady's view of what makes a great father

Tom Brady's children watched the person behind the NFL legend

Why football success was never the whole story for Tom Brady

Tom Brady is building a legacy beyond football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For much of his career, Tom Brady was defined by championships, records and an almost relentless commitment to football. Away from the stadium, however, another role has always carried a different kind of weight. As a father of three, Brady says his children have watched not only what he achieved, but how he worked for it. That lesson, he believes, may be one of his most meaningful legacies.Brady recently offered a personal look at fatherhood while reflecting on what life means beyond professional success. His message was not simply about spending time with children. Instead, he focused on the example parents set through their everyday choices."I think part of being a great father is being a great example of doing what it takes to take care of your family," he explained. "I chose to do it by playing football."For Brady, football was more than a career. It was also the way he showed his children the value of commitment, discipline and responsibility. The quarterback spent years building a routine around training, preparation and competition, often under enormous pressure."My dedication to the sport, the hours of practice, the moments when I was laser focused — those were times when I believe I was doing the best possible thing for my family and my kids, by prioritizing my profession and teaching, by example, what it takes to be really good at your job, what it takes to follow through on commitments, what it takes to be a great teammate; and showing them, also by example, that work is a big part of all of our lives. "That perspective adds another layer to Brady's famous career. The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star spent much of his adult life chasing excellence. His children were growing up while he was doing it.Rather than seeing those years only as sacrifices, Brady now views them as opportunities to demonstrate what dedication looks like.Brady is the father of three children. He shares his eldest son, John "Jack" Edward Thomas, with actress Bridget Moynahan. He shares daughter Vivian Lake and son Benjamin Rein with former wife Gisele Bündchen.His children have also experienced a childhood far removed from the ordinary. They watched their father compete on football's biggest stages, including Super Bowls, while also seeing the less glamorous side of professional sport. Early mornings, long practices, travel and recovery were all part of the picture.Brady believes those details matter."Remember, your children are watching everything. They see what you do in every aspect of your life and how you do it," he wrote. "Reading bedtime stories and helping them with homework are not the only ways to be a great parent."That does not mean Brady considers traditional parenting moments unimportant. His point is broader. Children learn from consistency. They notice how adults respond when things go wrong, whether promises are kept and how seriously they approach their responsibilities.For an athlete who built his reputation on preparation, those lessons naturally became part of his parenting philosophy.Brady also drew a clear line between sporting achievement and being a successful father."And neither is winning Super Bowls or MVPs," he continued. "Being a great football player didn’t make me a great dad, but how I became a great player certainly had an impact — from showing up day in and day out, to doing whatever it took to get better, be successful, be a role model, and to provide."It is a striking distinction from one of the most decorated careers in NFL history. Brady won seven Super Bowl titles and collected multiple individual honours, but his own definition of success as a parent does not rest on those achievements.Instead, he points towards the habits that helped him reach those heights.That message becomes especially relevant now that football no longer controls every part of his schedule. Brady has been able to devote more attention to family experiences, including holidays and trips with his children.His social media posts have offered glimpses of those moments. He has shared photographs with Jack, Vivian and Benjamin during family travels, including a European summer filled with sightseeing, time on the water and opportunities to experience different cultures.He also celebrated quieter moments. One photograph showed Vivian enjoying time in the water during a trip to Spain, prompting her proud father to call her his "little mermaid."The former quarterback's approach to fatherhood shows how dramatically the meaning of legacy can change after a sporting career.For decades, Brady's legacy was measured in wins, championships and statistics. Now, his own words suggest that the lessons he passes to his children matter just as much.His three children have seen the famous quarterback at work, but they have also seen a father who values preparation, persistence and responsibility. Those qualities can remain long after the final whistle.Brady's message is ultimately simple. Being present as a parent does not only mean being physically beside your children every moment. It also means giving them something to learn from.His football career provided the platform, but fatherhood gave those lessons a deeper purpose. Whether his children follow his path into sports or choose completely different careers, Brady appears to hope they carry forward the same principles: work hard, honour commitments, keep improving and show up for the people who matter.For a man who spent much of his life trying to become the best quarterback possible, that may be the most personal measure of success. His trophies tell the story of Tom Brady the athlete. His children, and the example he hopes to leave them, tell the story of Tom Brady the father.
Article Summary: Nfl legend tom brady is building a legacy beyond football. He says his children have watched not only what he achieved, but how he worked for it. Brady recently offered a personal look at fatherhood while reflecting on what life means beyond professional success.

Article Title: What happens to Carter Hart now? Hockey star’s ban upheld after acquittal, 4 players still suspended
Article Text:
Carter Hart. Image via: Bruce Bennett/ Getty Images

What happens to Carter Hart now?

Four players were acquitted in court, but their Hockey Canada suspensions remain in place

What Hart's 2028 World Cup eligibility could mean

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Carter Hart will remain barred from Hockey Canada programs through November 2027, even though a criminal court acquitted him of se*ual assault last year. An independent appeal board upheld that suspension on Wednesday, closing out a disciplinary process that ran separately from the courtroom case and outlasted it by more than a year.The ruling covers five players from Canada's 2018 World Junior team. Four remain suspended on staggered timelines, while a fifth was reinstated immediately. None of it affects their ability to play in the NHL, which conducted its own investigation and cleared all five to sign contracts again last year.Carter Hart, the Vegas Golden Knights goaltender, cannot participate in any Hockey Canada-sanctioned program until Nov. 10, 2027. That date falls just months before the 2028 World Cup of Hockey, the tournament's first edition since 2016, which sets up a real question about whether he could eventually wear the Maple Leaf again.His NHL path looks different. Hart signed a two-year, $4 million deal with Vegas last October and helped the Golden Knights reach the 2026 Stanley Cup Final before losing to the Carolina Hurricanes in six games. He posted a .909 save percentage and 2.56 goals-against average across 22 playoff appearances, numbers that outpaced every other Canadian goaltender in the postseason.The players, Hart, Michael McLeod, Dillon Dube, Cal Foote and Alex Formenton, were accused of se*ually assaulting a woman in a London, Ontario hotel room in 2018. All five were acquitted in July 2025 after a judge found the accuser's testimony not credible. Hockey Canada's own investigation reached a different conclusion on conduct, and the appeal board upheld it this week.Formenton was reinstated immediately. Foote's suspension runs through November 2026, Hart's through 2027, Dube's through 2028, and McLeod's through 2030. Officials have not explained why the timelines differ. Any of the four will also face an enhanced screening process, including a third-party review of the original findings, before Hockey Canada would consider them for a future roster.Canada's secretary of sport, Adam van Koeverden, framed the case as a turning point for the sport. "This case started a national conversation about safe sport," he said following the ruling, pointing to reforms Hockey Canada has made since the allegations first surfaced.Hart's on-ice case for a future recall is real. His regular-season numbers with Vegas last season were modest, an .891 save percentage over 18 starts, but he was working his way back after more than a year away from competitive hockey. The playoff run changed the conversation, and rival Canadian goaltenders like Colorado's Scott Wedgewood never matched his output.Selecting him would still be a hard call. The 2018 case drew national outrage, and Hockey Canada has spent years trying to rebuild trust through programs like Abuse Free Sport. The NHL, in its own July 2025 statement on the players, called their alleged conduct "unacceptable" even after the acquittals.Hart has kept his public comments focused on hockey rather than the case itself. "I'm just excited to move forward," he told reporters after signing with Vegas last fall.Whether that focus extends to a Team Canada jersey in 2028 depends on decisions Hockey Canada has not yet had to make.
Article Summary: Carter hart will remain barred from hockey canada programs through november 2027. An independent appeal board upheld that suspension on wednesday. The ruling covers five players from canada's 2018 world junior team. All five were acquitted in july 2025 after a judge found the accuser's testimony not credible.

Article Title: ‘Gambhir a fantastic coach’: Gary Kirsten backs under-fire India coach to deliver
Article Text:
File Pic: Gary Kirsten and Gautam Gambhir (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: India may be staring at the possibility of another setback in their World Test Championship campaign and that has increased the antagonism that cricket fans in India have towards head coach Gautam Gambhir . However, on Thursday, Gambhir found support from an old ally. Sri Lanka coach Gary Kirsten threw his weight behind the underfire India head coach, insisting that the former opener’s coaching credentials speak for themselves during a virtual media interaction.Kirsten, a former left-handed opener who coached India from 2008-11, cited Gambhir’s coaching record and said, “He’s a fantastic coach. He’s had incredible success. He has won a T20 World Cup (2026) and the ICC Champions Trophy (2025). He’s also had success in the IPL (Gambhir was the team mentor for 2024 IPL champs Kolkata Knight Riders). His record speaks for itself. I really enjoyed working with him when he was a player. He’s a smart cricketer and I knew he’d have success as coach.”Gambhir played under Kirsten when the South African was with the Indian team. He later coached South Africa (2011-13) and served as Pakistan’s head coach in white-ball cricket for six months in 2024.“It was a great three years and a privileged one to work with Indian players,” Kirsten said. “There was a lot of skill in that dressing room. What I appreciated was that they accepted me into their space and felt I could add value.I’ve approached the Sri Lankan role with the same seriousness.”Lately, India have shown a tendency to struggle against quality spin but Kirsten refused to reveal whether Sri Lanka would specifically target that weakness.Instead, he stressed that the hosts were focused on executing their own skills rather than obsessing over opponents.“We would like to bring all our skills into the game, not just spin,” he specified. “Whether you’re a seamer or a spinner, if you’re executing your skills properly, you’ll be in the game. We’ve done our homework on India and identified areas we may be able to exploit, but cricket unfolds session by session and you adapt accordingly.”The South African chose to be diplomatic when asked about India’s recent batting issues against spin. Instead, he kept steering the conversation back to Sri Lanka’s own preparation. “I’m not here to judge the Indian team,” he said. “They are a quality side with tremendous depth. Our responsibility is to make sure we’re ready, both in terms of skill execution and strategy. The focus remains on our strengths.”He also played down suggestions that Sri Lanka’s plans would revolve solely around left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya, whose remarkable record in Galle has earned him the nickname ‘King of Galle’. Jayasuriya has claimed 125 wickets in just 23 Tests, including 81 at the venue. “He’s a world-class bowler and he’s had great success at home,” Kirsten said. “But we don’t build our bowling strategy around one player. Every bowler has a role to play. It’s obviously great to have him in the mix though.”An unapologetic Test cricket-tragic who played in 101 Tests for the Proteas, Kirsten said he preferred longer Test series. “I’m a Test match purist. I love Test cricket. And my personal belief is that every country gets to play at least 10 Tests a year. I was very fortunate to be part of a South African team and to play over 100 Tests over a period of 11 years, which means you’ve got to play somewhere around 10 a year. There are challenges in the modern schedule, but it’s always great when your main Test-playing nations get to play a lot of Test cricket,” said the 58-year-old.Kirsten also welcomed Sri Lanka Cricket’s decision to allow free entry for spectators during the series, saying fuller stadiums create a far better experience. “It’s better to have people in the stadiums than no one,” he said. “I don’t know all the business implications, but from a cricket perspective it’s wonderful.”(Watch the India-Sri Lanka Test series live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)
Article Summary: Sri lanka coach gary kirsten throws his weight behind underfire india head coach gautam gambhir. Kirsten, a former left-handed opener who coached india from 2008-11, cited gambhier’s coaching record and said, ‘he's a fantastic coach. He's had incredible success’ kirsten also welcomed sri lanka cricket’s decision to allow free entry for spectators during the series.

Article Title: Intrigue around the Galle pitch but India likely to opt for the safe route
Article Text:
Indian players warm up during a training session ahead of the first Test cricket match against Sri Lanka at Galle International Stadium in Galle, Sri Lanka, on Thursday. (ANI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com in Galle:

If you bat first, make sure you go big. And if you bowl first, get the ball in the right area. So those disciplines are going to be important. Morne Morkel

Two days before the Test, there has been an unusual intrigue around the playing surface. Word from both camps is that it isn't the usual strip rolled out at Galle and may not turn as sharply as everyone expected before the series opener. It doesn't look like a dry, raging turner, and generous watering on Thursday suggests there are no attempts to crack it open on the opening day itself.Recent history suggests that for the first couple of days, Galle is a batting paradise, with gradual turn offered as the game progresses. Those who have seen it up close observed that it is a "good wicket," and India bowling coach Morne Morkel emphasised that "something will start to happen" as the match progresses."It looked like a good surface. And I think as the Test match will go on, something will start to happen. We've prepared basically for all that can come our way. And like I said, for us, it's more about the mental challenge now, facing these conditions, batting time, bowling those spells, and getting the ball in the right area," said Morkel during a media interaction."I think it's a good-looking surface on the eye. I'll be slightly surprised if it goes the other way.Traditionally, the first two days belong to the batting side. It's just crucial to get runs on the board. I think that's going to be important to whatever happens with the toss. If you bat first, make sure you go big. And if you bowl first, get the ball in the right area. So those disciplines are going to be important. And then from there, as the day's gone, obviously, assess and then come up with the best options for the day," he added.This leaves India with a crucial riddle to solve. Three spinners or three fast bowlers? As things stand, the former is a more reliable option, primarily because it adds batting depth, something head coach Gautam Gambhir is always averse to compromising. Ravindra Jadeja slots in as the premier all-rounder in the XI, while Mohammed Siraj is the leader of the fast-bowling pack. Kuldeep Yadav remains a no-brainer for this series, leaving two crucial spots to fill. While Prasidh Krishna is expected to narrowly edge Gurnoor Brar for the second pacer spot, Manav Suthar, who had an impressive one-off Test against Afghanistan, will give India that batting cushion at No. 8 and also add variety to the spin attack.If the spin attack remains as expected, it could be a rare instance where the visitors field all left-arm spinners, but this isn't currently bothering the Indian camp. Morkel asserted that all three are different from each other and it isn't a "massive concern" for the group."Kuldeep is an attacking bowler. Jaddu, with his experience and class, we can't look past. I think for us, they're all different in their ways. They're left-arm spinners, but what they do with the ball is slightly more accurate. I don't think it's a massive concern for us. It's just how Shubman is going to use those guys at certain times. In terms of skill, they've got the skill there to get the 20 wickets first," explained Morkel.The last Test at this venue was played between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in June 2025 and saw two 450-plus totals, four hundreds and four half-centuries. The hosts' leading spinner, Prabath Jayasuriya, went wicketless in the first innings, bowling 48 overs without success, and could only pick up one wicket in the second innings as well. Even in the two India A fixtures at the same venue last month, runs were on offer and fast bowlers enjoyed bowling.Gurnoor Brar, in particular, stood out with a 10-wicket haul in the second game.The youngster is very close to earning his Test cap as he continues to bowl with a lot of fire in the nets, and the team management is convinced that he is going to serve Indian cricket for a very long time, provided he remains fit. He hasn't left anything to luck or chance since arriving with the team in the first week of August. He bowled full tilt in Colombo, impressed in the warm-up game at the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground and bent his back in the first training session in Galle on Thursday. The wait, however, is expected to be slightly longer for the lanky quick.Even though much noise and chatter is expectedly on spin, Galle presents an opportunity for batters from both teams to capitalise on the first two days. For now, the teams will pray for a favourable toss, as the difference between first and fourth innings totals at this venue has been significant in the last few years. Winning the toss, batting first and batting big is going to be the mantra for success at this venue before the spinners can get a nice rip in front of the magnificent Galle Fort.

However, despite his recall, former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin believes Jurel is more likely to get the nod for the first Test, which begins on August 15.Sarfaraz, 28, has not played for India since the three-Test series against New Zealand (2024). He made a strong statement in the first Test with a 150-run knock, but failed to replicate that performance in the next two matches. He was subsequently left out of the playing XI during the Australia series and was later dropped from the squad altogether.The batter spent more than a year away from the Indian team, with questions surrounding the reasons for his exclusion. One of the reported concerns was his suitability and technique in overseas conditions.Ashwin, however, believes Sarfaraz deserves clarity from the team management if there are doubts about where he fits into India’s plans. According to the former spinner, captain Shubman Gill and head coach Gautam Gambhir should clearly communicate Sarfaraz’s role instead of leaving the batter uncertain about his future.“I'll start with Jurel. Sarfaraz came into the squad because of Sai Sudharsan's injury. The messaging is very important for Sarfaraz. If you feel he is a suspect in certain conditions, you need to give him clarity. You need to tell him that he can serve the team in sub-continental conditions," said Ashwin on his YouTube channel ‘Ash Ki Baat’.Ashwin feels Sarfaraz could carve out a significant role for himself in conditions where he is particularly comfortable, especially against spin.“So that way, even Sarfaraz won't waste his time on the rest of the things. He can focus on playing good spin, and he can become the king of the sub-continental conditions. He can build his career. If you feel he cannot work in certain conditions, then communicate that to him,” he added.A place for Sarfaraz in Galle could make sense given his ability to handle spin. The right-hander is comfortable using his feet against spinners and has shown an ability to keep the scoring rate moving by putting pressure on them.His sweep shot is another weapon that could prove useful in Sri Lankan conditions, allowing him to disrupt a spinner’s rhythm and force changes in length.Jurel, meanwhile, has produced mixed returns so far and did not make an impact during India’s warm-up game against SLC XI. That could add another layer to the selection debate, although Ashwin still expects the wicketkeeper-batter to be preferred.Sarfaraz’s experience of batting at No. 5 also means a move to No. 6 would not represent a major adjustment. Much of his domestic career for Mumbai and the West Zone has come in the middle order, where he has accumulated a huge volume of runs.With spin expected to play a major role in Galle, India face an interesting choice between Jurel and Sarfaraz. While Jurel appears to have the edge in Ashwin’s assessment, Sarfaraz’s record against spin and experience in the domestic game could make him a tempting option for the first Test.

Article Title: ‘Vaibhav Sooryavanshi doesn’t have that’: Ex-India great explains Rohit Sharma-Virat Kohli’s big edge
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh believes Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma should be allowed to continue their ODI careers and target next year’s World Cup if they retain the desire and fitness to do so, insisting that performance rather than age must determine their place in the team.Speaking to PTI, the 46-year-old former off-spinner weighed in on the ongoing discussion over the future of the two Indian veterans, who are now playing only one format. Harbhajan also revealed that his autobiography is complete and is likely to be released later this year.Harbhajan drew a comparison with Lionel Messi while making the case for Rohit and Kohli . Messi, at 39, led Argentina to the final of the recent football World Cup, producing moments of individual brilliance throughout the tournament.Rohit will be 41 and Kohli 39 when the 2027 ODI World Cup is played in South Africa. Harbhajan believes their age should not become a deciding factor if they continue to perform at the highest level."Whoever the player is, I believe the marker should be performance, not age," Harbhajan said.He feels the expectations surrounding Kohli and Rohit would be significantly greater than those on an inexperienced player such as Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, even though the teenager has already shown the ability to attack international bowlers." Virat may be 39 but if he is still beating those 20-year-old guys on the field, it (his age) doesn't matter. Look at Lionel Messi. At 40 (39), five men fail to stop him. If a player has that kind of fitness and skill where even five opponents can't keep him at bay, then we know that skill always takes precedence," he reasoned.Harbhajan also credited Kohli with changing India's approach towards winning, particularly during his time as captain from 2014-15 onwards. According to the former spinner, Kohli helped the team develop the belief that even seemingly impossible targets could be pursued rather than settling for draws."This change was first brought in by Virat Kohli when he became the captain in 2014-15. Before that we won't think that we can go for a chase of 400 on the final day. Virat told the boys, 'let's at least try. We might lose but if we keep trying one day we will surpass that 400 plus in last innings.'"'If we have to get 10 wickets on last day, we will go for it. The winning mentality and not settle for draw is what Virat Kohli got," he remembered.Kohli's impact, Harbhajan added, extended beyond tactics and results. He believes the former India captain was the biggest driving force behind the team's fitness transformation."But his biggest contribution was bringing in fitness culture. 90 per cent credit for creating the fitness revolution goes to Kohli. My idea of fitness was endurance but Virat made this team believe that if you are fit, you can fly around," Harbhajan pointed out.The former spinner therefore feels India head coach Gautam Gambhir should trust the experience of Rohit and Kohli if they continue to meet the required standards."If I were the coach, my job would be to give them the platform as my expectations from Rohit and Virat would be much higher than what I expect from a Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. These two have that experience. They have experience of 300 games which Sooryavanshi won't have. Yes, a Sooryavanshi can walk in and blast bowlers but Virat and Rohit have the experience," he explained.Harbhajan, who finished his international career with 416 Test wickets and 269 ODI wickets, maintained that fitness and performances should ultimately decide whether the veteran duo remain in contention."Fitness is a priority, and your performance matters. Performance is the ultimate criterion. So if these two score runs and can match the fitness of a Shreyas (Iyer) or a Yashasvi (Jaiswal), then nothing else matters," Harbhajan declared.The former India spinner also believes Rohit and Kohli themselves will know when their bodies and performances indicate that it is time to step away."Rohit and Virat will get their answer from within. You realise when you have reached that phase where you need to call time," he said.Harbhajan officially announced his retirement in December 2021, although his last Test appearance had come much earlier, in 2015 at Galle.
Article Summary: Former india spinner harbhajan singh believes virat kohli and rohit sharma should be allowed to continue their odi careers. The 46-year-old former off-spinner drew a comparison with lionel messi while making the case for rohit and kohli. He also revealed his autobiography is complete and is likely to be released later this year.

Article Title: Prichard Colon death at 33: Terrel Williams’ ‘rabbit punches’ revisited as doctor explains Colon’s irreversible brain damage
Article Text:
Prichard Colon death at 33: Terrel Williams’ ‘rabbit punches’ revisited as doctor explains Colon’s irreversible brain damage

What happened to Prichard Colon after the Terrel Williams fight?

Why did Prichard Colon never recover from his brain injury?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Puerto Rican boxer Prichard Colon died at 33 on August 13, nearly 11 years after the 2015 fight that left him with a severe brain injury. Colon suffered repeated punches to the back of his head during his bout with Terrel Williams in Virginia. He later underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain and spent 221 days in a coma. After waking, he remained severely disabled and needed constant care from his family. His death has renewed attention on the injury and why his condition never returned to normal despite years of care.The injury happened during the October 17, 2015, fight at EagleBank Arena in Fairfax, Virginia. Colon complained to referee Joe Cooper about punches to the back of his head, which are illegal in boxing. The World Boxing Council later described these blows, known as rabbit punches, as dangerous because they can damage the area where the spine connects with the brainstem.The fight continued into the ninth round, when Terrel Williams knocked Colon down twice. Colon’s corner then removed his gloves, apparently believing the fight was over. Because he could not answer the bell for the next round, the bout was stopped and Williams was declared the winner by disqualification.After leaving the ring, Colon became dizzy and later vomited and collapsed in the dressing room. He was taken to hospital and underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain.The World Boxing Council said Colon suffered a subdural hematoma and irreversible brain damage from the rabbit punches. He eventually came out of the 221-day coma but was left with severe, permanent problems and could not return to his previous life.Dr. Jason R Williams, a California-based oncologist, explained the possible effect of the injury in a post on X. He wrote: “Those punches landed where the spine meets the brainstem, and the skull barely covers that spot,” Williams wrote on X. “The bleed that started there had nowhere to go. Trapped blood builds pressure. Pressure kills brain tissue.“Brain tissue does not come back. Surgeons saved his life that night, but no treatment in medicine could return what the bleed took. He spent 221 days in a coma and the next decade unable to walk or speak, while his parents cared for him around the clock.“Prichard did what a fighter is supposed to do,” he continued. “He reported the fouls to the one person who could stop them. It didn’t save him. That part has never left me.“Boxing learned from him. In 2016 the WBC put a zero-tolerance rule on those punches and named it after him. Fighters are safer today because of what he lost. Once brain damage runs this deep, we cannot treat our way out of it. Prevention is the only cure.”The WBC later formalised the Prichard Colon Rule, calling for stricter action against rabbit punches.A cause of death for Colon has not been publicly announced. His father, Richard Colon, announced his death on August 13 and said he was in a “happy place now.”
Article Summary: Prichard colon suffered repeated punches to the back of his head during his bout with terrel williams in virginia. He later underwent emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain and spent 221 days in a coma. After waking, he remained severely disabled and needed constant care from his family.

Veteran Sri Lankan cricket coach and former school mentor Sumith Fernando has died following an altercation involving young players at a cricket facility in Colombo. Fernando, 62, passed away on Tuesday while undergoing treatment at a hospital after sustaining injuries during the incident on August 8. The coach remembered for mentoring several young cricketers, including current Sri Lanka ODI captain Kusal Mendis during his school days.According to PTI, the incident began when a group of young cricketers training at a sports facility went to get drinking water but found that there was no running water available. A disagreement reportedly broke out between the players and stadium staff over the issue. Fernando, who was present at the venue and had also worked as a curator at the Bloomfield Cricket & Athletic Club, intervened as the situation escalated.Police said a physical confrontation subsequently took place involving two players. A 17-year-old school cricketer was allegedly involved in the altercation, during which Fernando sustained injuries. He was rushed to Colombo National Hospital for treatment but died on Tuesday while receiving medical care.Police arrested the 17-year-old player on Monday on suspicion of assaulting Fernando. Since the accused is a minor, he was placed under child probation custody after being produced before a Colombo court on Tuesday.His custody has reportedly been extended until August 17 as the investigation continues.Fernando was a former coach at Prince of Wales College in Moratuwa and played a significant role in the development of several school-level cricketers. Among those he coached was Mendis, who went on to become Sri Lanka's ODI captain. Fernando later served as a grounds curator at Bloomfield Cricket & Athletic Club, a prominent club in Sri Lanka's domestic cricket structure.Fernando's funeral was held on Thursday.

Article Title: Brittany Mahomes shares emotional Chiefs camp family moment as Patrick Mahomes continues intense comeback

Brittany Mahomes turned a routine Kansas City Chiefs training camp day into a memorable family moment when she brought her three children to support Patrick Mahomes. Sterling, Bronze and Golden joined their mother at Missouri Western State University on August 4, giving the quarterback a welcome break from the intensity of his NFL comeback. The sweet family visit comes as Patrick prepares for another season after a major knee injury.Brittany, Patrick's wife and a Kansas City Current co-owner, arrived at training camp with their three children: 5-year-old Sterling Skye, 3-year-old Patrick "Bronze" Lavon and 1-year-old Golden Raye.The family outing quickly became more than a simple visit. Wolf, the Chiefs mascot.The images captured the lighter side of training camp. Patrick spent much of the day focused on football, but his children gave him a chance to step away from the demands of practice and enjoy time with his family.Sterling embraced the Chiefs theme in a red cheerleader-style outfit featuring her name. Bronze wore a Chiefs shirt, while Golden sported a gold onesie with "Mahomes" across the front.Brittany kept her look relaxed in Adidas clothing.One of the most touching moments came when Patrick was surrounded by all three children on the field. The family moment stood in sharp contrast to the intense work taking place around them.Brittany captioned her Instagram carousel with red and yellow heart emojis, while Patrick responded in the comments with a red heart.The visit also showed how closely the Mahomes family remains connected to Patrick's football career. For the children, training camp can be an exciting chance to see their father at work. For Patrick, having his family nearby offers a reminder of life beyond the field.The family visit came shortly after Patrick opened up about how becoming a father has changed the way he views training camp.Now 30 and entering his 10th NFL season, Mahomes has reached a point where he understands that his football career will not last forever. Fatherhood has encouraged him to appreciate moments that might once have seemed insignificant.“You have to enjoy the moments... To have that different perspective, now being a father is to enjoy the little moments and enjoy the time at camp, enjoy the cafeteria, because all of a sudden you’re going to look up, you’re not going to be coming back here,” the Chiefs quarterback said.Those comments add meaning to the family's appearance at camp. He kept playing; he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice,” Reid told CBS Sports host Evan Washburn, adding, “he’s all in.”Reid also praised Mahomes as an example for his teammates, saying he is willing to do whatever is necessary to get back on the field.“He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid said.With the 2026 season approaching, Mahomes has plenty to prove physically. Yet his family's presence at training camp offers another perspective on his comeback.Football remains the priority when Patrick steps between the lines. But moments with Brittany, Sterling, Bronze and Golden are becoming just as valuable.For the Mahomes family, a day at Chiefs training camp became more than a football outing. It became a small family memory, exactly the kind of moment Patrick now says he wants to appreciate while he still can.

Article Title: How could Maxx Crosby’s top 25 ranking change the Cowboys’ 2026 trade plans?
Article Text:
Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby was voted the No. 24 player on the NFL Top 100 for 2026. (Image via Getty)

What does Maxx Crosby's No. 24 ranking say after a turbulent offseason?

Why are the Cowboys still being linked to Maxx Crosby?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maxx Crosby is still a Las Vegas Raider. His peers also still see him as one of the NFL's best players. Neither fact has stopped another round of trade speculation.Crosby landed at No. 24 on the NFL Top 100 for 2026, the league announced Thursday. It marks his fifth consecutive appearance on the player-voted list and his fourth straight year inside the top 25. The ranking comes five months after a proposed trade to the Baltimore Ravens collapsed and with the Dallas Cowboys once again being mentioned as a possible destination.Crosby dropped only two places from No. 22 in 2025. More importantly, his production gives players plenty of reason to keep him inside the NFL's top tier.The five-time Pro Bowler finished the 2025 season with 10 sacks despite missing Las Vegas' final two games. He also recorded 28 tackles for loss, second in the NFL behind Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. Crosby led the Raiders in sacks, tackles for loss and quarterback pressures while tying for the team lead with six pass deflections, according to Raiders.com.Those numbers came during a season in which Crosby underwent another heavy workload before having meniscus surgery.The knee became a major part of his offseason for another reason.Las Vegas agreed in March to send Crosby to Baltimore for two first-round picks, but the deal never became official. ESPN reported that the Ravens backed out after medical concerns arose during Crosby's physical. Crosby remained with the Raiders, while Baltimore eventually moved elsewhere for pass-rush help.Five months later, Crosby is back on the field in Las Vegas and back inside the NFL Top 100's top 25.Raiders defensive line coach Travis Smith pointed to the habits behind that production when discussing Crosby.“The people around him are so fortunate, including coaches, to watch the routine and the discipline he approaches every day with,” Smith said, via Raiders.com.Crosby is also the second Raiders player on the 2026 list. Tight end Brock Bowers came in at No. 60.The placement offers a useful snapshot of how players around the league view Crosby after the trade saga and knee questions. He may have slipped two spots, but they still ranked him ahead of several established stars, including T.J. Watt, Chris Jones, Aidan Hutchinson and Jalen Carter.His standing around the NFL does not appear to be the uncertain part of his situation.His long-term home might be.Dallas already tried to get involved once.ESPN reported in March that the Cowboys offered Las Vegas the No. 12 overall pick as part of their pursuit of Crosby before the Ravens emerged with their two-first-round-pick package. The Cowboys ultimately moved in another direction after failing to land the Raiders star.Now, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has revived the possibility of Dallas circling back.During an appearance on “Yahoo Sports Daily,” Florio said a Crosby trade could become realistic if Las Vegas struggles once the regular season begins.“I can see a team like the Cowboys,” Florio said. “They’ve already talked about giving up future assets to improve their defense. And there was talk that they were thinking about making a play for Maxx Crosby back in March when the Ravens did. It would not surprise me if the Cowboys contend, the Raiders don’t, Crosby gets traded to Dallas.”That is speculation, not a report that Las Vegas is currently shopping Crosby or that Dallas has made another offer.There is also an obvious reason the idea continues to surface. Crosby has already shown what his trade market could look like. Baltimore was prepared to surrender two first-round picks before the physical stopped the deal, and Dallas had its own talks with Las Vegas earlier in the offseason. ESPN's reporting from March established that there was real interest, not simply a hypothetical connection between a contender and an elite pass rusher.Crosby now enters the season healthy enough to participate in Raiders training camp, removing at least some of the uncertainty that surrounded his knee in March.Las Vegas has no reason to treat a trade as inevitable. Crosby remains its top defensive player, and his No. 24 ranking is another reminder of his value.But the offseason already proved something important. A Maxx Crosby trade went much further than rumor once.That is why every time another contender needs a pass rusher, the conversation is unlikely to stay dead for long.
Article Summary: Las vegas raiders edge rusher maxx crosby was voted the no. 24 player on the nfl top 100 for 2026. It marks his fifth consecutive appearance on the player-voted list and his fourth straight year inside the top 25. The ranking comes five months after a proposed trade to the baltimore ravens collapsed.
